guidance.evidence_criterion: Read the complete definition together with every route by which information becomes confidential and any operative confidentiality duty. For explicit identification, support requires a marking, designation, or confirmation regime applicable to the covered disclosures; oppose when confidentiality can instead arise from nature, context, reasonable understanding, or unmarked categorical inclusion. A mixed rule with an identification route and an alternative context-based route opposes an assertion that all information must be expressly identified. For technical-only scope, oppose whenever any non-technical category is expressly included; do not infer technical-only status from examples or silence. For oral information, support only when oral or verbal disclosure is covered directly or through a confirmation procedure; broad references to information, generated material, or communications alone do not establish oral coverage. For confidentiality of the agreement or its negotiation, require language covering the existence, terms, negotiations, communications, or contractual arrangements of this agreement plus an applicable confidentiality obligation; discussions about a different prospective relationship do not suffice. Use NotMentioned when the exact form or subject is unsettled. Cite all definition branches and operative provisions necessary to establish the boundary, including independently annotated categories, but not unrelated examples.

operations.rationale: Creates a definition-and-form procedure because observed errors confused broad definitions with identification duties, inferred oral coverage from generic categories, and missed negotiation confidentiality; the contrasts also require complete definition evidence.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Separate the two acquisition routes. Independent development concerns creation by the receiving party without use of, access to, reference to, or reliance on protected information. Third-party acquisition concerns receipt from a person entitled to disclose and not bound by confidentiality. An exclusion from the definition or confidentiality obligations can support the corresponding permission even if phrased as an exception rather than an affirmative grant. Do not use third-party receipt to support independent development or vice versa, and do not infer either route from a general public-domain or prior-possession exception. Support when the matching route is expressly available, oppose when it is expressly forbidden, and otherwise return NotMentioned. Cite the exception lead-in when it supplies the legal effect and every matching condition needed to show the route and its limits.

operations.rationale: Creates a reusable exception procedure after the lawyer treated third-party receipt as independent development in one source and repeatedly omitted exception lead-ins or qualifications.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Identify the receiving actor, the expressly permitted recipient class, the information disclosed, and every need-to-know, purpose, approval, or confidentiality condition. Employee sharing is supported only by a clause authorizing access or disclosure to employees; third-party sharing is supported by an affirmative permitted class such as agents, representatives, consultants, advisers, or other non-employees. A permission limited to employees does not support third-party sharing. A general nondisclosure rule that never addresses the relevant class is unresolved, while an exclusive recipient list that omits the class, an express prohibition, or a regime allowing outsiders only through case-specific discloser approval opposes a standing permission. Do not treat responsibility for a recipient's breach as itself permission to disclose. Cite the operative permission or exclusion, its recipient class, and all provisions imposing necessary conditions; include separately operative recipient provisions when independently relevant.

operations.rationale: Creates a recipient-class procedure because sharing had the highest relation confusion: employees, agents, outsiders, approval-only disclosure, and general bans were repeatedly conflated, with many original members omitted.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Analyze return or destruction, creation of copies, and post-disposition retention as separate actions. A termination-based return/destruction statement is supported only when termination, expiration, or failure to consummate the contemplated arrangement itself activates the duty; a demand-only duty, or a termination clause effective only if a later request is made, does not establish that proposition. For copying, require an affirmative right to reproduce or copy in identified circumstances. A prohibition on copying, including one liftable only by case-specific consent, opposes that permission; a right to retain an existing archival copy or a command to return copies does not prove a right to create one. Post-disposition possession is supported only by an express archival, legal-compliance, backup, infeasibility, or similar retention carveout that operates after the return/destruction obligation. An exhaustive duty covering all materials and copies with no carveout opposes retention; silence is unresolved. Cite the trigger, operative action, covered objects, and each exception or qualification that changes the result, excluding merely contextual disposition language not part of the original decision boundary.

operations.rationale: Creates a lifecycle procedure because request-only duties were mistaken for termination duties, retention was inferred from timing, and archival copies were mistaken for permission to create copies.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Match the exact actor, action, and object rather than treating all restrictive clauses alike. Limited use is supported by a sole-purpose authorization or an express ban on every other purpose; resolve any defined purpose and cite it when needed, together with all independently operative use restrictions. No licensing is supported by language denying licenses, title, interests, or other rights in the protected information; ownership language and a no-grant clause should both be cited when they jointly state the rule. A reference preserving rights under a separate agreement does not itself mean this NDA grants them. Oppose only if this agreement affirmatively grants the relevant right. Reverse engineering requires language specifically prohibiting or permitting reverse engineering, decompilation, disassembly, or an equivalent examination of objects embodying the information. Do not infer it from limited-use, nondisclosure, ownership, no-license, copying, or general security provisions. If the exact action is not settled, return NotMentioned.

operations.rationale: Creates an action-specific procedure to preserve consistently correct limited-use and licensing relations while repairing pervasive evidence incompleteness and preventing broad restrictions from being extended to reverse engineering.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Locate a legally compelled disclosure trigger and determine whether the receiving party must communicate with the disclosing party before or promptly upon disclosure. Notice, advance consultation, or a required opportunity to contest can support the duty even without the word 'notify'; cooperation or disclosure-limitation language alone cannot. A compelled-disclosure exception with no communication duty is unresolved, and an express authorization to disclose without notice opposes. Cite the operative communication duty and include its lead-in only when needed to establish that the duty applies to protected information compelled by law, regulation, court, or governmental process. Include separate contest or timing language only when it is part of the annotated duty.

operations.rationale: Creates a trigger-and-notice procedure because advance consultation was missed in one source and evidence selection varied between self-contained duties and clauses needing a governing lead-in.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Determine whether any contractual obligation, rather than merely a right or factual condition, continues after termination or expiration. Support an express survival sentence, a fixed post-termination duration, or language stating that confidentiality or non-use continues. If the survival clause names or cross-references particular sections, inspect those sections and cite the operative obligations together with the survival language; if a broad survival clause is self-contained, cite that clause without importing unrelated provisions. Do not infer survival merely because the agreement has a term, permits later retention, or lacks a termination release. Oppose an express termination of all obligations; otherwise use NotMentioned when post-termination effect is unstated.

operations.rationale: Creates a survival-scope procedure because labels were correct but underlying obligations and cross-referenced sections were repeatedly omitted from otherwise correct evidence.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Require an operative restriction on the receiving party soliciting, enticing, inducing, recruiting, or hiring identified employees or other representatives of the disclosing party. Verify the protected class, prohibited conduct, purpose, duration, and any consent exception. A restriction on contacting information sources, disclosing names, using confidential information, or communicating with representatives is not a nonsolicitation covenant unless it addresses solicitation or equivalent recruitment conduct. Support an applicable prohibition, oppose an express permission to solicit, and otherwise return NotMentioned. Cite the complete operative covenant and any clause defining its protected class or material exception.

operations.rationale: Creates a narrow nonsolicitation procedure to preserve the sole observed positive boundary and prevent unrelated contact or confidentiality restrictions from expanding it.
